question: Why did NO emissions keep rising all the way up to 80% NH3 blending?

The document does not explicitly state why NO emissions kept rising all the way up to 80% NH3 blending. However, it does mention that at 20% NH3 blend, NO decreases by about 40% relative to pure coal firing, likely due to the combined effects of selective noncatalytic reactions of NH3 and heterogeneous NO reduction by char. 

At higher NH3 blending ratios, NO emissions increase monotonically with NH3 loading, but at 80% NH3, NO declines again, plausibly because excessive NH3 decomposition consumes thermal energy and perturbs the conversion pathways from elemental combined nitrogen to NO.
